claims.claim: Crown Castle's 2026 revenue contraction is substantially explained by identifiable tenant cancellation shocks rather than a demonstrated collapse in underlying leasing demand: February guidance expected $240 million of DISH/Sprint termination and cancellation impacts while comparable organic contribution excluding those impacts remained positive.

The July 2026 outlook still placed full-year site-rental revenue about 5% below 2025 while AFFO per share was guided about 5% higher, showing that balance-sheet repair and cost/interest relief can improve cash-oriented performance even before headline rental revenue recovers.

DISH's January 2026 payment default and network exit is direct evidence that tenant concentration can produce discontinuous cash-flow and contract-realization risk even when tower infrastructure remains operationally useful.

risks.risk: Tenant concentration can create abrupt revenue and contract-realization losses when a major carrier exits or defaults.
AFFO improvement driven partly by financing and cost relief should not be interpreted as proof that site-rental growth has already normalized.

contradictions.contradiction: Improving AFFO per share coexists with declining site-rental revenue because debt reduction, interest savings and operating efficiencies can offset tenant cancellation pressure.

unknowns.unknown: The pace at which post-DISH/Sprint organic leasing can offset cancellation losses remains unproven until subsequent operating periods establish sustained net growth.

falsifiers: If subsequent periods show comparable organic leasing weakening materially after cancellation effects normalize, the interpretation that current contraction is primarily a discrete churn shock should be revised.
If AFFO growth persists only through cost/interest relief without renewed site-rental growth, resilience improves but the organic-growth thesis remains unverified.
